job.title: Registered Nurse / Enrolled Nurse / AIN – Casual Aged Care
job.description:
Registered Nurses, Enrolled Nurses & Personal Care Workers | Residential Aged Care | Sunshine Coast, QLD

Collarcare is one of Australia's leading aged care recruitment agencies, partnering with reputable Residential Aged Care providers across Queensland.

We're looking for compassionate and experienced Registered Nurses (RNs), Enrolled Nurses (ENs) and Personal Care Workers (PCWs) to join our casual workforce across the Sunshine Coast and surrounding areas, QLD.

Whether you're looking for extra shifts, greater flexibility, or the opportunity to work across multiple facilities, Collarcare gives you the freedom to choose shifts that suit your lifestyle.

Why Join Collarcare?

  • Competitive agency rates $$$
  • Flexible shifts to suit your lifestyle
  • Choose your own shifts through our easy-to-use online portal
  • Work with reputable aged care providers across the Sunshine Coast
  • Supportive recruitment team dedicated to your success
  • Ongoing opportunities across a variety of facilities
  • A workplace that genuinely values your wellbeing and work-life balance

About the Roles

As an RN, EN or PCW, you will play an important role in providing safe, high-quality and person-centred care while supporting residents to maintain their independence, dignity and quality of life.

Registered Nurses – Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver comprehensive clinical and person-centred nursing care
  • Administer medications and monitor residents' health and wellbeing
  • Complete accurate clinical documentation and care plans
  • Conduct assessments and ongoing clinical reviews
  • Work collaboratively with GPs, allied health professionals, residents and families
  • Ensure compliance with the Aged Care Quality Standards and organisational policies

Enrolled Nurses – Key Responsibilities

  • Provide safe and person-centred nursing care under the direction of an RN
  • Administer medications and monitor residents' health and wellbeing
  • Complete clinical documentation and contribute to care planning
  • Monitor and report changes in residents' condition
  • Support residents with their daily care and clinical needs
  • Work collaboratively with RNs, PCWs and the wider care team

Personal Care Workers – Key Responsibilities

  • Provide personal care and support to residents with daily living activities
  • Assist with mobility, nutrition, hydration and personal hygiene
  • Support residents' dignity, independence and overall wellbeing
  • Observe and report changes in residents' health and behaviour
  • Maintain accurate documentation and follow care plans
  • Work collaboratively with nurses and the wider care team

About You

Registered Nurses

To be successful, you will have:

  • Current AHPRA Registration as a Registered Nurse
  • Previous experience working in an Australian Residential Aged Care facility (clinical placements are not considered)
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification
  • Current National Police Check (within the last 12 months)
  • NDIS Worker Screening Check (or willingness to obtain)
  • Evidence of current COVID-19 vaccination, including booster where required
  • Current Influenza vaccination
  • Valid Australian working rights
  • 100 points of identification

Enrolled Nurses

To be successful, you will have:

  • Current AHPRA Registration as an Enrolled Nurse
  • Previous experience working in an Australian Residential Aged Care facility (clinical placements are not considered)
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification
  • Current National Police Check (within the last 12 months)
  • NDIS Worker Screening Check (or willingness to obtain)
  • Evidence of current COVID-19 vaccination, including booster where required
  • Current Influenza vaccination
  • Valid Australian working rights
  • 100 points of identification

Personal Care Workers

To be successful, you will have:

  • Certificate III or Certificate IV in Individual Support, Ageing Support, or a relevant equivalent qualification
  • Previous experience working in Australian Residential Aged Care
  • Current CPR and First Aid certification
  • Current National Police Check (within the last 12 months)
  • NDIS Worker Screening Check (or willingness to obtain)
  • Evidence of current COVID-19 vaccination, including booster where required
  • Current Influenza vaccination
  • Valid Australian working rights
  • 100 points of identification

Apply Today

job.description:
Maintenance Officer – ACT

Full-Time Opportunity | ACT

Collar Care is currently seeking an experienced Maintenance Officer to join a well-established aged care organisation in the ACT.

This is a hands-on role responsible for supporting the delivery of reactive and preventative maintenance, ensuring buildings, property and equipment are maintained to a high standard and that a safe environment is provided for residents, staff and visitors.

What’s on Offer

  • Pay Rate: Up to $35 per hour + 12% Super
  • NFP benefits
  • Full-time opportunity
  • Stable and rewarding work environment
  • Opportunity to work within an established aged care setting

About the Role

You will be responsible for:

  • Completing preventative and reactive maintenance
  • Undertaking general handyman and building maintenance
  • Maintaining property, buildings and equipment
  • Responding to maintenance requests in a timely manner
  • Coordinating and overseeing contractors when required
  • Identifying and escalating maintenance risks
  • Supporting compliance with relevant standards and WHS requirements
  • Maintaining accurate records relating to maintenance, consumables and expenses

The role is focused on maintaining a safe, functional and high-quality living environment for residents, staff and visitors.

job.title: Educator - Bowral
job.description:
Clinical Educator

Harbison 
View all jobs
Burradoo, Southern Highlands & Tablelands NSW
Nursing - Educators & Facilitators (Healthcare & Medical)
Full time
$60 – $61.39 per hour
Posted 3d agoLow application volume

How you match
Matches based on your career history
Aged Care

Microsoft Office

Show all?

Are you passionate about developing people, strengthening clinical practice and improving outcomes for older people?

Harbison is looking for an experienced and engaging Clinical Educator to help shape the capability of our workforce across both residential and community care. This is an opportunity to take the lead in building a strong culture of learning—where education goes beyond compliance and translates into confident staff, better practice and better outcomes for the people we support.

As Harbison continues to grow and diversify its services, you will have the opportunity to influence how we develop our workforce for the future, working alongside clinical and operational leaders to turn evidence, quality insights and best practice into meaningful learning that makes a difference every day.

Harbison Overview

Harbison is a charitable, community-owned, not-for-profit organisation that provides residential and non-residential care and support services for aged or disabled people, including a range of support services and systems to assist aged and disabled people to achieve maximum independence and integration within a residential or community setting, education and training of professionals and other care providers, and activities which are incidental or conducive to these objectives.

Harbison offers community focused educational programs, such as its intergenerational program, and has added childcare services through its subsidiary, Harbison Early Learning Pty Ltd (HEL) to its portfolio of programs. HEL is an approved childcare provider.

Currently, Harbison is an approved aged care provider, retirement village owner, and one of the largest employers in the Southern Highlands. Harbison is governed by a Board of Directors which appoints a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) who is delegated with day-to-day responsibility for the organisation.

Primary Purpose of the Role

The Clinical Educator provides strategic leadership for clinical education, workforce capability and competency across both residential care and community care at Harbison. The role is responsible for ensuring that education programs support the delivery of safe, effective, evidence-based and person-centred care that meets the requirements of the Aged Care Act 2024, the Strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards and other relevant legislation and professional standards.

Working collaboratively with operational leaders, the Clinical Educator develops and oversees a contemporary clinical education framework that supports the ongoing development of a capable, confident and competent workforce. The role ensures education is informed by organisational priorities, quality and clinical governance data, emerging evidence and best practice.

The Clinical Educator provides professional leadership to the Workplace Trainer and works closely with managers and subject matter experts to ensure learning is translated into everyday practice. Success in this role is demonstrated through improved workforce capability, measurable improvements in care quality, positive consumer outcomes and a culture of continuous learning and improvement.

Equal work opportunities

At Harbison, we do not discriminate against, a person's cultural background, heritage, disability, age, gender, or sexuality. Harbison believes in equal work opportunity for all workers and candidates.

Benefits

  • Salary packaging includes up to $15,900 in pre-tax earnings plus $2,650 to contribute towards entertainment benefits each year.

  • Access to in-house and online training programs.

  • Career progression opportunities.

  • Supportive, positive team environment.

Requirements - Essential

  • Current registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA.

  • Certificate IV in Training and Assessment (TAE40122 or current equivalent), or willingness to obtain.

  • Demonstrated experience in clinical education within aged care, health or community services.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of the Aged Care Act 2024, Strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards, Statement of Rights, and Aged Care Code of Conduct

  • Strong understanding of clinical governance, quality improvement and adult learning principles.

  • Demonstrated ability to design, deliver and evaluate competency-based education programs.

  • Highly developed coaching, facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Strong organisational, analytical and project management skills

  • High level of digital literacy, including Learning Management Systems and Microsoft Office applications.

If this opportunity interests you, we'd love to hear from you. Simply upload your resume and cover letter, and we'll send you the full Position Description by email.

Please note the current Influenza vaccination is a requirement of employment at Harbison.

COVID-19 vaccinations are highly recommended.
